scope: Splicery pure Lean calculus and authority component; not an SG02 or SG03 gate pass

obligations.property: Exact byte cuts and validated half-open ranges decompose the immutable original; invalid bounds refuse without clamping.
positive_examples: Splicery.cut_of_parts proves a nonempty exact decomposition.
Splicery.cut_eof and the EOF Core examples accept a zero-width cut at input length.
Bounded oracle cases 00, 01 and 02 accept exact replacements, empty-input insertion and EOF deletion.
negative_examples: Core examples reject reversed, over-EOF and over-width cuts.
Bounded oracle cases 03 through 08 reject bad offsets, widths and encodings.
Splicery.Surface.surfaceCut_rejects_reversed and surfaceCut_rejects_overflow reject invalid independent-surface bounds.

obligations.property: A splice is exactly prefix, replacement and suffix; exterior bytes are unchanged, keep is identity and length is exact.
positive_examples: Splicery.apply_local exposes the exact output decomposition.
Splicery.keep_identity proves a selected original span can be copied unchanged.
Bounded oracle case 00 returns 61585863 from input 616263.
negative_examples: Splicery.applyAt_eq_none_iff propagates cut refusal with no partial output.
Bounded oracle cases 03 and 04 reject invalid widths rather than preserving a guessed suffix.

obligations.property: Replace, delete, before and after lowering execute with the same denotation as the primitive splice.
positive_examples: Splicery.lower_correct covers all four Command constructors, including insertion at EOF through Core.applyAt_eof.
negative_examples: Primitive refusal remains governed by Splicery.applyAt_eq_none_iff; no lowered candidate is asserted for an invalid cut.
The after-to-start control distinguishes insertion after the selected bytes from insertion at their start.

obligations.property: Reads and targets use the authorized immutable image, with origin and capability checks; stale or read-only captures cannot become writable.
positive_examples: Splicery.Surface.readCapture_original derives the exact original source slice for every successful read.
Splicery.Surface.selectedCut_sound derives the original-image decomposition for every accepted target.
negative_examples: Stale-image, image-read-only and target-read-only examples in Surface.lean return none.
Splicery.Surface.target_refusal_no_candidate rules out both direct and lowered candidates after target refusal.

obligations.property: Canonical batches validate positions, refuse every overlap without partial output, preserve original gaps and are permutation independent.
positive_examples: Splicery.swap_authored_from_original and swap_from_original derive a two-span swap with an arbitrary untouched gap.
Splicery.applyAuthored_eq_of_perm derives equal output for valid disjoint permutations.
negative_examples: The four not_compatible theorems cover intersection, coincident insertions and insertion at replacement boundaries.
Splicery.canonical_no_partial_result and applyAuthored_none_iff expose no partial candidate.

obligations.property: Source-order lexical scopes, complete frozen matcher evidence and anchor/line selectors (`between`, `from … to`, `whole`) enforce cardinality, ordering, profile and budget refusal before a candidate; every selection is one checked plain [lo,hi) region.
positive_examples: Splicery.Surface.freeze_members and frozen_complete_membership preserve the complete checked inventory and scope.
Surface nonvacuity examples derive a singleton frozen set and source-order references.
Surface examples select whole CRLF, LF and unterminated final lines (to EOF) and from/to spans covering both anchors; Differential vectors 12-whole and 13-from-to agree with the Rust preview.
negative_examples: Duplicate/shadowed binders, empty needles, incomplete or truncated evidence, wrong cardinality, raw profile and excess work all refuse.
Surface examples include zero, ambiguous and over-budget selections.
whole of a non-line capture and reversed, coincident or overlapping from/to anchors refuse.

obligations.property: Enabled payload and selector productions preserve exact bytes and text boundaries; direct surface denotation refines to primitive execution or refuses.
positive_examples: Splicery.Surface.lowerChange_end_to_end covers direct denotation through primitive execution for all Change constructors.
Quoted, heredoc, raw-hex, lines-like and indent examples in Surface.lean include present-empty payloads and exact CRLF retention.
negative_examples: Invalid UTF-8 candidates, malformed escapes/hex and invalid text boundaries return none in the Surface examples.
Splicery.Surface.invalid_text_candidate_refuses prevents a candidate rejected by the text oracle.

obligations.property: Domain-separated prepared identity binds every input field; live grants, exact active scope and supported current profiles are required without evidence-based authority gain.
positive_examples: Splicery.preparation_admits_current_exact derives admission from a live grant, exact active scope and current supported profiles.
Splicery.claim_accepts_live_exact_request derives a claimed state from that admission and the exact edit-preparation identity.
negative_examples: Changed inputs cannot reuse an identity; read and edit identities cannot share a domain.
Read-only or stale-generation grants, foreign-run aliases and refused stale/unsupported profiles cannot authorize preparation.
Receipts and citations cannot widen authority; changed identity refuses a claim.

obligations.property: Pure preparation is deterministic, bounded and effect-free; guarded claim/observation/replay transitions and separate file-operation preconditions admit only exact derivations.
positive_examples: Splicery.preparePure_success_exact_candidate returns the exact stamped candidate and an empty effect list within budget.
Exact observations confirm or reconcile; identical request-key replay retains its outcome.
Create, rename and remove each have a nonvacuous admitted precondition derivation.
negative_examples: Budget excess returns budgetExceeded with no effects; changed same-key intent conflicts.
Wrong preimages refuse confirmation and matching after bytes alone cannot reconcile.
Create requires absence and literal-only content, rename requires regular source, absent destination and one filesystem, and remove requires a regular source.

trusted_assumptions: Bytes are finite immutable lists; host adapters supply exact input provenance and range-check unbounded Lean naturals before allocation.
CanonicalEncoder.encode_injective is a reviewed premise; a digest instantiation must prove DigestEncoder.digest_collision_free rather than infer it from collision resistance alone.
TextOracle.valid_sound and boundary_sound are instantiated by the named strict UTF-8 decoder and exact boundary implementation.

Matcher evidence is trusted only after freeze checks origin, scope, completeness, non-truncation, cardinality and conservative work accounting; leftmost-first regex semantics and unique lexer group declarations remain external.

PreparationPolicy and Grant represent current host evidence for active schema, supported profiles, exact scope, generation and write capability; namespace and run separation are structural equality checks.
Native create/rename/remove observations, exclusive reservation, current active grant, metadata and a cooperating exclusive worktree are adapter inputs, not proved physical facts.
Exact recipe-origin spans, heredoc delimiter extraction and all host resource charges are supplied and checked outside the pure calculus.
Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are permitted standard logical axioms, each subject to the producer's per-declaration printed-axiom audit.
excluded_host_claims: No SG02 or SG03 gate pass is asserted; SG00/SG01 receipts for SG02 and the SG02 receipt for SG03 must be established by their own producers and release aggregation.
No physical filesystem, path containment, descriptor race, durability, atomicity, fsync, ledger or OS authorization theorem is claimed.
No production Rust authority/preparation implementation is claimed by the empty L08 production_rust_symbols mapping; host wire and IO integration remain excluded.
No cryptographic digest implementation or canonical wire serialization is proved merely by the encoder premises.
No parser correctness for edited source, semantic equivalence of user programs, regex-engine correctness or physical resource usage follows from these pure theorems.
The bounded primitive oracle and calibrated mutants are component evidence, not full host-wire conformance or release qualification.
